content.title: About
content.content: Congee with egg is a traditional Asian comfort food consisting of a thick rice porridge cooked until the grains break down, with a boiled egg added for protein. Warm, soothing, and easy to digest, it is commonly served for breakfast or a light dinner.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Any rice variety can be used, but short‑grain rice is most common because it breaks down quickly.
In China congee is often topped with ginger, scallions, soy sauce, or pickled vegetables.
The egg is added at the end of cooking so the whites set while the yolk stays soft.
The dish is considered a “comfort food” and is frequently given to people recovering from illness.

items.title: Source of easily digestible carbs
items.content: Rice in congee provides quick‑release energy, helpful for recovery after sickness.

items.title: Rich in protein
items.content: The egg supplies complete protein needed for tissue growth and repair.

items.title: Contains B‑vitamins
items.content: Both rice and egg deliver B1, B2, and B6 vitamins that support metabolism and nervous system function.

items.title: Gentle on the stomach
items.content: The soft texture makes it suitable for people with sensitive digestion.

items.title: Hydration
items.content: The high liquid content helps maintain the body’s water balance.

items.title: Egg allergy
items.content: Individuals allergic to eggs should avoid this version of congee.

items.title: High glycemic index
items.content: Rice porridge can raise blood sugar quickly, so people with diabetes should monitor portion size.

items.title: Sodium content
items.content: If soy sauce or broth is added, the sodium level may become high.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Serve congee hot, optionally topping with soy sauce, sliced scallions, ginger, or a drizzle of oil. The egg can be left whole, sliced, or stirred into the porridge.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Refrigerate leftover congee in an airtight container for up to 2 days. Reheat with a splash of water or broth to restore the desired consistency.
